title: P0.26: External Failure Context Continuity
description: When an external consultation is blocked, the next user message about that same block must inherit the failure context before normal route selection. If the user offers to help with verification or says their own Chrome is already authenticated, IABV must distinguish the program's isolated profile from the user's browser profile and avoid repeating the blocked profile.
reason: Live runtime evidence showed ChatGPT was correctly selected and blocked by browser security verification. P0.26 prevented the 120s local timeout and opened a visible window, but the window was still visible_isolated_profile. The user then authenticated in their normal Chrome and IABV repeated the same isolated-profile block. The missing step was profile reconciliation: user-browser session != IABV isolated session.
dependency_missing: LIVE_PROOF: run IABV on Windows, trigger ChatGPT security verification, say that Chrome is already authenticated / the opened window was wrong, then request ChatGPT again.
next_action: After restarting IABV with this slice loaded, reproduce the profile mismatch. Expected: IABV opens the user's default browser, records profile_mismatch_detected, switches the next retry to user_browser_manual handoff, copies the prompt, and does not repeat the isolated session block.
resume_hint: P0.26/P0.27/P0.28 extends the existing P0.16 external failure follow-up guard with security-verification vocabulary, visible window handoff, profile-mismatch detection, user-browser/manual handoff, and OSES findings for repeated external-failure continuity loops.

metadata.universal_algorithm_lesson: Before deciding a new route, preserve the causal context of the immediately previous failure AND the identity of the resource being used. A browser window is not a browser session; profile identity is part of the world model. If the user authenticates a different profile, switch to a governed user-browser/manual or CDP path instead of repeating the isolated profile.
